Employees traveling for approved business purposes may claim reasonable transportation, lodging, and
meal expenses. Travel must be approved by the employee's manager before booking. Expense claims
should be submitted within 15 calendar days after returning from the trip.

Business meal expenses are reimbursable when directly related to approved business activities.
Employees must provide itemized receipts and identify the business purpose and participants.

All expense claims must be reviewed and approved by the employee's reporting manager. Claims above
$2,500 require additional approval from the Finance Department. Expenses without sufficient
documentation may be rejected.

A purchase order is required before committing to purchases above $1,000 unless an approved
exception applies. Employees should use authorized suppliers whenever possible.

Corporate credit cards are issued to approved employees for authorized business expenses.
Cardholders must retain receipts and submit monthly expense reports. Personal purchases using a
corporate card are prohibited.

Full-time employees are eligible for 24 days of paid annual leave per calendar year. Employees should
submit leave requests through the employee portal at least five working days before the planned leave.
Emergency leave may be requested through the manager when advance notice is not possible. Unused
annual leave may be carried forward for up to 10 days into the following calendar year.

Employees are eligible for 12 days of paid sick leave per calendar year. A medical certificate may be
required for absences lasting more than three consecutive working days. Employees should inform their
manager as early as possible when they are unable to attend work because of illness.

The standard working schedule is Monday through Friday, from 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM, including a
one-hour lunch break. Employees working flexible schedules must agree on working hours with their
manager. Repeated unexplained absence or lateness may result in disciplinary action.

Employees participate in a formal performance review twice each year. Performance discussions cover
objectives, delivery, collaboration, professional development, and areas for improvement.

Eligible employees may work remotely up to two days per week with manager approval. Employees
must maintain availability during agreed working hours and use company-approved collaboration and
security tools.

Employees must use strong passwords for company accounts and must not share passwords with
colleagues. Passwords should contain a combination of letters, numbers, and special characters where
supported.

Multi-factor authentication is mandatory for critical company systems and remote access services.
Employees must register an approved authentication method and promptly report suspected
unauthorized access.

Employees accessing internal company resources from outside the corporate network must use the
company-approved VPN. Remote access credentials must be protected and should never be shared.

Company laptops and mobile devices must use approved security controls, including screen locking and
endpoint protection. Employees must report lost or stolen devices to the IT Service Desk immediately.

Employees may install software only when it is approved by the IT Department or provided through
approved software distribution systems. Unauthorized software is not permitted on company-managed
devices.

Suspected phishing emails, malware infections, accidental data disclosure, and unauthorized access
must be reported immediately to the IT Security team.

Business contracts must be reviewed by the Legal Department before signature when they create
material financial, regulatory, intellectual property, or liability obligations. Employees must not sign
contracts without appropriate delegated authority.

Employees must protect confidential company information and may disclose it only to authorized
individuals with a legitimate business need. Confidential information includes business plans, customer
information, trade secrets, and non-public financial information.

Personal data must be collected, processed, stored, and shared in accordance with applicable privacy
laws and company procedures. Employees should access personal information only when necessary.

Employees must disclose actual or potential conflicts of interest to their manager or the Compliance
Department. A conflict may arise when personal interests could improperly influence business decisions.

Work products created by employees as part of their employment responsibilities may belong to the
company according to applicable agreements and laws. Employees must respect third-party copyrights
and licenses.

Employees are encouraged to report suspected violations of law, company policy, or ethical standards
through approved reporting channels. Retaliation against individuals who raise concerns in good faith is
prohibited.
